question: Is HDC a cascade of A-N classes (H_a), a substrate-specific instantiation of an info-theory primitive (H_b), or one of fourteen flat co-equal classes (H_c)?
user_load_bearing_observation: Bronze antikythera is a discrete-state computational substrate (like silicon BSC). The bronze's 'HDC equivalent' ops (gear-mesh / positional-sum / dial-shift / position-diff) look NOTHING like silicon HDC ops (XOR / popcount-majority / ROL / Hamming), yet operate on the same kind of substrate.

decompositions.bind: Class I (Z/2 add) circ Class B (bit addr) circ Class C (iterate)
decompositions.bundle: Class C (stream-sum) circ Class J (threshold-compare) circ Class B (bit addr)
decompositions.permute: Class I (cyclic-shift on Z/D) circ Class B (bit addr) circ Class C (iterate)
decompositions.similarity: Class C (sum) circ Class J (popcount) circ Class I (Z/2 add) circ Class N (rational normalise)

verdict: Implementation-level decomposition succeeds for all 4 ops. Per the dissolve-before-promote default of [[feedback_no_privileged_primitive_classes]], this is necessary-but-not-sufficient for H_a. Identity-question remains: does the composite STRUCTURE (4 ops together) carry identity beyond per-op decomposability?

bronze_substrate_ops.bind: gear-mesh coupling: Z/n_teeth component-wise addition via differential gear-train (Class I + Class L)
bronze_substrate_ops.bundle: N-gear differential train sum + integer-divided averaging (Class I + Class L + Class J)
bronze_substrate_ops.permute: per-component cyclic-shift on Z/n_teeth (pure Class I)
bronze_substrate_ops.similarity: total-budget cyclic-group distance normalised to [-1, +1] (Class I + Class L + Class N)

anomaly_investigated_and_resolved: First bronze similarity formula used arithmetic-mean of per-component similarities; gave 0.0 where silicon BSC gives -1.0 for antipodal Z/2. Total-budget normalisation (sum_k|delta_k| / sum_k floor(m_k/2)) is the correct generalisation: reduces to silicon BSC on Z/2 and gives s=-1 for max-distance positions on any Z/n.
structural_finding: Silicon BSC is the Z/2-restricted special case of a general Z/n cyclic-group HDC family. Z/2 has 3 special properties: (1) bind is self-inverse (XOR a a = 0), (2) every vector has a true antipode (bit-complement), (3) random-vs-random similarity centered on 0. General Z/n loses (1) and (3); (2) survives for even m via m/2-shift.
verdict: Bronze antikythera CAN perform HDC-equivalent computation using ONLY Class I + Class L + Class J + Class N primitives. NO 'Class M_bronze' needed. The bronze ops realise the SAME information-content functions (encode-aggregate-permute-compare) as silicon BSC's bitwise ops.

claim: Spike #30A's 14-flat-co-equal-classes vocabulary stands as the algebraic-operational partition
supporting_evidence_from_spike_36: H_a per-op decomposition is necessary-but-not-sufficient — same finding as Spike #30A noted in the per-class table: M's sub-ops decompose to other classes, but the composite structure (M-as-a-whole, 4 ops together with their algebraic relations) retains identity at the operational level

H_b confirms bronze HDC IS substrate-portable cyclic-group HDC; the bronze sub-ops decompose to I+L+J+N, exactly mirroring silicon BSC sub-ops decomposing to I+B+C+J+N. Both substrates instantiate the SAME information-content function with substrate-specific implementations.
Cross-class survey: all 14 classes A-N have parallel info-theoretic identities AND substrate-specific implementations. Class M is NOT singular in this regard.
verdict: H_c stands as the algebraic-operational partition. The Spike #30A finding (14 flat co-equal classes) is preserved. What Spike #36 adds: an INFO-THEORY OVERLAY is available across the full 14-class vocabulary, parallel to the existing partitions per [[user_stance_partition_for_understanding]].

ssot_canonical_shannon_1948_citation: Shannon (1948) 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication', Bell System Tech. Journal 27, July 379-423 + October 623-656. Verified via Wikipedia citation + freely-available PDFs at Harvard Mathematics + Internet Archive Bell Laboratories collection.
verdict: Class M's 4 ops correspond exactly to Shannon's 4 canonical channel operations. This is not coincidence — HDC was conceived as a vector-symbolic-architecture realisation of Shannon-channel coding; the 4 ops ARE Shannon's primitives by construction (Plate 1995 / Kanerva 1988 / 2009).

Per [[user_stance_identity_not_implementation_discipline]]: class identity at the info-theory level; class implementations are substrate-specific.
Class_M_specifically: EXPLICITLY confirmed substrate-portable in HDC literature: same VSA framework realised on silicon (BSC), DNA (ACGT), optical (HRR), neural (SDM). Bronze antikythera adds a fifth substrate to the list — same info-content function via gear-mesh / differential / per-component-shift / cyclic-position-difference primitives.

Class M is one of fourteen flat co-equal classes at the algebraic-operational partition level; the parallel info-theoretic / substrate-portable framings are additional partitions, not class additions. The user's intuition (the bronze does HDC differently from silicon) is CORRECT and is honoured by the substrate-specificity finding — the substrate-specific implementations vary; the information-content function is invariant.

intuition: Bronze antikythera does HDC operations differently from silicon, yet operates on the same kind of discrete-state substrate. Is HDC therefore (a) a cascade of A-N classes, (b) a substrate-specific instantiation, or (c) flat-class with substrate-specific implementations?
verdict: (b) AND (c) are BOTH true at different ontological levels. (a) is true at the implementation level but does not collapse the composite identity. The MPM-discipline test ([[user_stance_partition_for_understanding]]): each partition can be true at its level without competing with the others.
specific_finding_load_bearing_to_intuiti: The bronze HDC analog REQUIRES general Z/n cyclic-group arithmetic (Class I expanded beyond Z/2); silicon BSC operates at the special Z/2 restriction. This is a real algebraic distinction with consequences: bronze bind is invertible-via-subtraction (not self-inverse); bronze similarity has cyclic-group baseline ~1/m for random vs random (not centered on 0). The information-content function (Shannon channel coding) is the same; the algebraic group structure is broader on bronze.

remaining_falsifiers: Demonstrate a Class M operation that cannot be decomposed into A-N + I+L+J+N composition (would falsify H_a + H_b together).
Find a substrate where HDC-equivalent computation is INCOMPATIBLE with cyclic-group primitives (would suggest Class M is sui generis and substrate-portable in a way not captured by Class I cascade).

Identify a class A-N that does NOT admit a parallel info-theory identity (would falsify the uniform-overlay claim — the overlay would be partial, suggesting some classes are NOT info-theoretic primitives).

Cross-class survey: are there OTHER classes whose 'binding-layer' or 'wrapper' surface might actually be a substrate-portable channel-coding primitive (cf. Class M)? — e.g., Class D (dispatch) as Huffman-coding-shape, Class E (catalog) as Shannon dictionary, Class B (TLV) as source-frame. These were surveyed positively here; deeper formalisation could expose disconfirming counter-examples.

anomalies_found.anomaly: First bronze_similarity formula gave 0.0 on Z/2 antipodal where silicon BSC gives -1.0
anomalies_found.investigation: Arithmetic-mean of per-component similarities vs total-Hamming-vs-D normalisation. Per-component max distance for Z/2 is 1; (1 - 2*1/2) = 0, NOT -1.
anomalies_found.resolution: Corrected to total-budget normalisation: 1 - 2*sum_k|delta_k|/sum_k floor(m_k/2). On Z/2 with K=D components: sum_k floor(m_k/2) = D; sum_k|delta_k| = hamming. Formula reduces to silicon BSC exactly.
anomalies_found.verdict: Real signal not noise. Identified a structural Z/2-special property of silicon BSC: total-budget vs per-component-mean is the key distinction for cross-substrate algebraic generalisation.

anomalies_found.anomaly: Random Z/17 similarity converges to ~0.50, NOT to 0 like silicon BSC
anomalies_found.investigation: For uniform random on Z/m: E[|delta_signed|] = m/4 approximately. E[comp_sim] = 1 - 2*(m/4)/m = 1/2 for any odd m. This is NOT a bug; it's a real cyclic-group property: silicon's Z/2 has the special expected-similarity-0-for-random property because Hamming/D = 1/2 for random bits gives 1 - 2*(1/2) = 0.
anomalies_found.resolution: Document as Z/2-special-property finding. Generalisation to Z/n shifts the expected-random-similarity baseline. Has implications for HDC noise tolerance on non-Z/2 substrates.
anomalies_found.verdict: Real structural finding. Bronze HDC (general Z/n) has different signal-to-noise ratio properties than silicon BSC (Z/2). Cross-substrate HDC engineering would need to account for this.

DNA HDC concrete: ACGT base-4 alphabet IS a Z/4 cyclic group; bind = (codon a + codon b) mod 4 by-position; similarity = Hamming-on-Z/4 normalised. Already in HDC literature (Kanerva 2009, Najafabadi et al 2018). Could be added to bronze and silicon as a third substrate confirmation.

Optical HDC concrete: Plate 1995 HRR uses complex-valued vectors with circular convolution for bind; permute = phase shift; similarity = inner product real part. Already in HDC literature. Adds an optical-substrate concrete to the substrate-portability claim.

Implication for srmech.amsc.hdc API: consider exposing a SUBSTRATE PARAMETER (Z/2 default for silicon BSC; user can pass moduli=(n1, n2, ...) for general bronze-style cyclic-group HDC). This would make srmech's Class M API the substrate-portable HDC primitive across all five substrates surveyed.
